answer: Registration mints a relic only after an oracle stamps one hundred days of verified service, and the relic is carved into a marble plinth the issuer hardware writes once and cannot re-etch. Entry costs a base levy of sixty POA plus a fixed surcharge for every identity a household already holds, burned at minting. Unverified relics earn nothing, and a forged plinth voids the identity and its escrow. So across an ocean of sybils, k identities still demand k plinths, k surcharges and k hundred-day waits, keeping marginal cost linear in n.
